sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: your driving privilege and other important information: points, habitual offenders, occupational licenses, reinstatement, seat belts, child seats and insurance
Audience: every first-time Wisconsin Class D applicant, and especially probationary drivers, whose points can be doubled.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the chapter sets the point, habitual offender and occupational license rules [A01], the test accessibility options and the seat belt law [A02], and the child seat, insurance and fuel-saving guidance [A03].
Level: number-heavy rule recall with several similar thresholds over different time windows; moderate load.
Prerequisites: the license progression section on probationary licenses and the dangerous driving behaviors section on impaired driving.

corpus_stability.reason: The Wisconsin Motorists Handbook prints 2026 on its front cover and form number BDS126 with 2026 on its back cover; it is a yearly-dated handbook with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
